briefs.legalName: Petition to Vacate a Misdemeanour or Gross Misdemeanour Conviction, RCW 9.96.060(2)
briefs.publicName: Vacate a Washington misdemeanour conviction after three clean years
briefs.mechanism: Washington vacates; it does not expunge adult convictions. On a granted petition the court permits withdrawal of the guilty plea and entry of a not guilty plea, or sets aside the guilty verdict, then dismisses the charging document and vacates the judgment and sentence. The applicant must have completed all terms of sentence including satisfaction of financial obligations; at least three years must have passed since the later of release from supervision or probation, release from total and partial confinement as defined in RCW 9.94A.030, or the sentencing date; and there must be no new crime in this state, another state or federal or tribal court in the three years before the application. Since 2024 c 296 the three-year clock no longer restarts on the date legal financial obligations are paid off, and the court may be asked to cancel or reduce some of them. Relief is discretionary: the court may in its discretion vacate even where every requirement is met, which makes Washington unusual and means no outcome may be promised. On vacation the person is released from all penalties and disabilities, the conviction is not included in criminal history for later sentencing, and for all purposes including employment and housing the person may state they were never convicted.
briefs.venue: The sentencing court: the district or municipal court that imposed the misdemeanour or gross misdemeanour sentence. There is no transfer to a higher court.

briefs.publicName: Vacate a Washington drug conviction after treatment or a recovery programme
briefs.mechanism: Added by 2023 sp.s. c 1 s 11 as part of the post-Blake drug legislation and absent from the internal reference altogether. A person convicted under RCW 69.50.4011(1)(b) or (c), 69.50.4013, 69.50.4014, or 69.41.030(2)(b) or (c) qualifies on either of two paths: completing a substance use disorder programme and filing proof of completion with the court; or obtaining an assessment from a recovery navigator programme under RCW 71.24.115, an arrest and jail alternative programme under RCW 36.28A.450, or a law enforcement assisted diversion programme under RCW 71.24.589, together with six months of substantial compliance with recommended treatment or services and progress toward recovery goals as reflected by a written status update. There is no waiting period; the six months of compliance is the only clock and only on the second path. The outcome is mandatory: upon verification the court must vacate the conviction or convictions. Subsection (6) is drafted as a standalone route and does not on its face incorporate the subsection (2) exclusion list.
briefs.venue: The sentencing court for the conviction or convictions to be vacated.

destination.name: Clerk of the sentencing court
destination.detail: File the petition with the programme documentation. The outcome is mandatory upon verification, so the packet's job is to make verification easy: the documentation, the statute of conviction and the cause numbers, assembled once.

briefs.legalName: Application to Vacate a Pre-1975 Treaty Indian Fishing Rights Conviction, RCW 9.96.060(4)
briefs.publicName: Vacate a pre-1975 Washington fishing conviction where a treaty right was being exercised
briefs.mechanism: A mandatory route reaching misdemeanour, gross misdemeanour and felony convictions alike, notwithstanding RCW 9.94A.640, which is broader than the internal reference's footnote treatment. It applies to a conviction before 1 January 1975 of violating any statute or rule regarding the regulation of fishing activities, including the enumerated former fisheries and game statutes, where the person claimed to be exercising a treaty Indian fishing right. The court must find two things: that the applicant is a member of a tribe that may exercise treaty Indian fishing rights at the location where the offence occurred; and that the state has been enjoined from enforcing the statute or rule to the extent it interferes with a treaty Indian fishing right as determined under United States v. Washington or Sohappy v. Smith and any post-trial orders, or any other state supreme court or federal court decision. On those findings the court shall vacate. The person may apply, or, if the person is deceased, a family member or an official representative of the tribe of which the person was a member may apply on their behalf.
authority: United States v. Washington, 384 F. Supp. 312 (W.D. Wash. 1974)
Sohappy v. Smith, 302 F. Supp. 899 (D. Or. 1969)
briefs.venue: The sentencing court. Because the route reaches felonies as well as misdemeanours, that may be a superior court.

destination.detail: File the application in the sentencing court. Where the subject of the conviction has died, the applicant may be a family member or an official representative of the tribe, and the packet is prepared in that person's name.

briefs.legalName: Participant Request that the Supervising or Detaining Authority Issue and Forward the Certificate of Discharge (Wis. Stat. § 973.015(1m)(b))
briefs.publicName: Ask for the certificate that completes your expungement
briefs.mechanism: Section 973.015(1m)(b) makes issuance mandatory rather than discretionary: upon successful completion of the sentence the detaining or probationary authority SHALL issue a certificate of discharge, which shall be forwarded to the court of record and which shall have the effect of expunging the record. The triggering event is successful completion — no subsequent conviction and, where the person was on probation, no revocation and satisfied conditions. Where that mandatory certificate was not issued, or was issued but never forwarded to the clerk, the participant may write to the supervising or detaining authority asking that it be issued and forwarded. No statute or rule prescribes the contents of that request and Wisconsin publishes no official participant form for it, so the correspondence is drafted. The letter supports implementation of an expungement the court already ordered; it does not itself change legal status, and the certificate remains the authority's document.
briefs.venue: Not a court filing. The request is addressed to the supervising or detaining authority for the participant's own case, which is statewide in scope: the Department of Corrections in most probation cases, or the detaining authority where the sentence included confinement.

destination.name: The detaining or probationary authority that supervised the participant, with the clerk of circuit court as the certificate's destination
destination.detail: The letter goes to the supervising or detaining authority, because § 973.015(1m)(b) places the issuing and forwarding duty on it. It asks that the certificate of discharge be issued and forwarded to the clerk of the circuit court of conviction, and asks the authority to confirm when that has been done. A copy to the clerk of circuit court is appropriate where the participant has already confirmed with the clerk that nothing was received.

briefs.legalName: Motion to Dismiss the Charges and Application to Expunge After a First-Offence DUI Deferral, W. Va. Code § 17C-5-2b(c) and (g)
briefs.publicName: Clear a first DUI that was deferred and dismissed after the test and lock program
briefs.mechanism: Read at source on 2026-08-06, § 17C-5-2b operates on a person who pleads to or is found guilty of the offence defined in § 17C-5-2(e), has no prior DUI-type conviction, and notifies the court within 30 days of arrest of the intention to participate in a deferral. On those conditions the court, without entering a judgment of guilt, shall defer further proceedings and place the person on probation conditioned on successful completion of the Motor Vehicle Alcohol Test and Lock Program under § 17C-5A-3a, for at least 165 days after a 15-day licence suspension and completed within one year thereafter. The section then creates two separate participant-facing submissions. First, under subsection (c), when the defendant has satisfactorily completed the programme and complied with its conditions, the defendant may move the court for an order dismissing the charges; that motion must be supported by the defendant's affidavit and by certification of the Division of Motor Vehicles that the programme was successfully completed, and the prosecuting attorney has 30 days after service to advise the judge of objections, in the absence of which the court shall dismiss. Second, under subsection (g), after a period of not less than one year beginning to run immediately on the expiration of the term of probation, the person may apply to the court for an order expunging all official records of the arrest, trial and conviction, except those maintained by the Division of Motor Vehicles, provided that a person previously convicted of a felony may not make that motion; objections are filed within 30 days of service, and if objections are filed the court holds a hearing and, if it determines there was no serious or repeated violation of the conditions of probation, it shall order the expungement. Only one discharge and dismissal is available under the section, and § 61-11-25(a) independently provides that no Division of Motor Vehicles record may be expunged by virtue of any order entered pursuant to § 17C-5-2b.
briefs.venue: The court in which the § 17C-5-2(e) charge was brought and which deferred proceedings and imposed probation. Both units are filed in that court.

destination.name: Clerk of the court that deferred proceedings and imposed probation under § 17C-5-2b
destination.detail: Both units are filed with the clerk of the court that entered the deferral. Unit 1 is served on the prosecuting attorney, who has 30 days to object. Unit 2 is filed no sooner than one year after the probation term expired and is likewise served on the prosecuting attorney, who has 30 days to object, with a hearing if objections are filed. Neither order reaches any Division of Motor Vehicles record.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Division of Motor Vehicles certification of successful completion of the Motor Vehicle Alcohol Test and Lock Program
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: West Virginia Division of Motor Vehicles
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the Division of Motor Vehicles for written certification that you successfully completed the test and lock program. Section 17C-5-2b(c) requires the motion to dismiss to be supported by this certification, so it must be attached before you file that motion.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Order deferring proceedings and imposing probation
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court that entered it
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for a certified copy of the order deferring the proceedings and placing you on probation. It carries the probation term the one-year expungement clock is measured from.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Order of dismissal and discharge
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court that entered it
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for a certified copy of the order dismissing the charges and discharging you.

participantFilingRequirements.name: Written confirmation of the date the probation term expired
participantFilingRequirements.obtainedFrom: The probation office that supervised the participant, or the clerk of the court
participantFilingRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the supervising probation office, or the clerk, for written confirmation of the date your probation term expired. This date, not the dismissal date, starts the one-year period.

selfHelpStopConditions: The charge is live and the participant has not yet notified the court of an intention to participate in a deferral. The 30-day notification window is charge-stage criminal defence, is outside scope, and closes quickly; the participant needs a lawyer immediately.
The participant holds a commercial driver's licence or operates commercial motor vehicles.
A court entered an order finding that the participant refused the secondary chemical test.
The participant's licence had previously been revoked for a same-elements offence in any jurisdiction.
Any other offence under the serious traffic offences article was charged in the same prosecution.
The participant has any prior felony conviction, which bars the subsection (g) expungement motion outright.
Anyone has alleged a serious or repeated violation of the conditions of probation, or the prosecutor files objections and the court sets a hearing.
The participant did not complete or was removed from the test and lock program.
The participant is chiefly concerned about the driving record, which this route never clears.
Firearm rights, immigration consequences, professional licensing, commercial driving, or federal, tribal, military or out-of-state records questions.

Hard limit that must be disclosed: no Division of Motor Vehicles record may be expunged by virtue of an order entered pursuant to this section. The criminal record can be cleared; the driving record cannot.
Compute the one-year window from the expiration of probation, not from the dismissal.

Section 17C-5-2b(g)(1) also provides that any person who has previously been convicted of a felony may not make a motion for expungement pursuant to the section. The controlling review does not record this bar; it is asked as a threshold question on this route as it is on section 61-11-25.

What LegalEase cannot complete: the Division of Motor Vehicles certification that the test and lock program was successfully completed. The participant obtains it and attaches it to the motion to dismiss, which section 17C-5-2b(c) requires it to support.

What LegalEase cannot complete: the court's finding on probation violations. If the prosecutor objects, the court holds a hearing on whether there was any serious or repeated violation of probation conditions, and automated assistance ends there.

waitingPeriods.condition: Motion to dismiss the charges, § 17C-5-2b(c)
waitingPeriods.duration: None beyond satisfactory completion of the Motor Vehicle Alcohol Test and Lock Program and compliance with its conditions. The programme itself runs for at least 165 days after a 15-day licence suspension and must be completed within one year thereafter.

waitingPeriods.condition: Application to expunge, § 17C-5-2b(g)(1)
waitingPeriods.duration: Not less than one year, beginning to run immediately upon the expiration of the term of probation. The clock runs from the expiration of probation, not from the dismissal.

exclusions: Any prosecution in which any violation of any other provision of article 17C-5 has been charged, § 17C-5-2b(f)(1).
Any person who holds a commercial driver's licence or operates commercial motor vehicles, § 17C-5-2b(f)(2).

Any person who has previously had a licence to operate a motor vehicle revoked for an offence with the same elements under a municipal ordinance of this state or any other state, or a statute of the United States or any other state, § 17C-5-2b(f)(3).
Any person as to whom a court entered an order finding a refusal of the secondary chemical test under § 17C-5-7a, § 17C-5-2b(f)(4).
Any person previously convicted of a felony, who may not make the subsection (g) expungement motion.
Any person who has already had one discharge and dismissal under the section, § 17C-5-2b(e).
Any Division of Motor Vehicles record, which the expungement order expressly does not reach.
The deferral request itself, made within 30 days of arrest, which is charge-stage criminal defence and is expressly outside the adopted LegalEase product scope.
